nodes.description: External view function randomMod that derives a pseudo-random number and returns it modulo mod.
Caller-supplied seed value mixed into the keccak256 randomness computation.
Caller-supplied nonce value mixed into the keccak256 randomness computation.
Caller-supplied modulus applied to the hashed randomness result.
Origin address of the transaction, attacker-influenced and used as randomness entropy.
Current block timestamp, miner/validator-influenceable and used as randomness entropy.
keccak256 over abi.encodePacked(tx.origin, nonce, blockhash, block.timestamp, seed) reduced modulo mod; weak on-chain randomness that is predictable/manipulable.

edges.reason: tx.origin is read directly as entropy in the randomness hash, letting the transaction origin influence and predict the pseudo-random output.
block.timestamp is used as randomness entropy, making the result dependent on manipulable block-level state.
seed parameter is encoded into the keccak256 input of the randomness operation.
nonce parameter is encoded into the keccak256 input of the randomness operation.
mod parameter controls the modulo reduction applied to the generated hash.
randomMod executes the hashing and modulo operation as its return expression.

normalization_plan.reason: The seed parameter has no independent on-chain state; it is only consumed as input to the unsafe randomness operation, so it collapses into that core unsafe_operation node.
The nonce parameter is only used inside the randomness hash and carries no persistent semantics, so it merges into the core unsafe_operation node.
The mod parameter only parameterizes the modulo reduction inside the randomness operation, so it merges into the core unsafe_operation node.
